- The plant typically grows to a height of 10-20 feet (3-6 meters) and has a spread of 8-12 feet (2.5-3.5 meters).
- Its leaves are dark green and ovate, and the plant produces clusters of small yellow flowers in the early spring, which are followed by bright red berries in the fall.
- The Korean Cornel Dogwood is used in traditional medicine to treat a variety of ailments, including arthritis, diarrhea, and fever.

description:
Red Osier Dogwood (Cornus sericea) A.k.a. American Dogwood. Large, native shrub that grows 1.5–4 meters tall in wet ground, along banks of rivers, creeks, ponds, and marshes. Twigs are purplish-red, strigose or villous. Leaves elliptic to ovate or lanceolate, bases obtuse or rounded, secondary veins 4–7 on each side of blade, prominent beneath, surfaces abaxially pubescent, adaxially strigose, Petioles 6–30 mm. Inflorescences flat-topped with many-branched cymes, strigose or villous, hairs. Flower corollas white to cream. Fruits ellipsoidal, 7–9 mm, white, seldom bluish. Peak bloom time: May–September. There are several subspecies.

description: More then 4 bracts on the flowers higher in the tree. Often the blooms are inaccessible, but there were some to be smelled and looked at down low. This is the last 1/5th of a large and diverse forest that was between 75-140 years old (spent time to count some tree rings). It was likely logged before during the turn of the century. The w.r cedar, Doug fir, western hemlock and pacific dogwood, was cut last year and the slash piles were covered until this spring. They have begun harvesting another portion of this on the NE side of this parcel. One large section was cleared, burned, disked, and they had a sprayer on trailer to complete 1/3 of the project where it was disked. I believe this all belongs to Rice Rock Museum as there property sits on harvested areas. As for this and 3 other dogwoods in this little patch left near there house and driveway, it would be safe to assume they are keeping it for ‘aesthetic’ and highway noise reasons. Very diverse forest compared to plenty in the region. I will be in touch with the owners or lumber company to see if I can do any permissed salvaging.
